title: Kids' commercial bands and first job at the St. Maurice Avenue theater
summary: Early bands played collegiate arrangements, then a silent-movie trio at a dollar a night.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I would say that it was kind of commercial in the very beginning because we had little bands like the kids do today. They get together in the homes, you know, and they get little arrangements, you know. They were already writing little specialized arrangements like on college songs, you know, collegiate, collegiate, yes, we're all collegiate, and yes, that's my baby, and all those sort of tunes, Charleston and those things were beginning to come out. And they had little arrangements on them, and of course most of the kids read a little bit, and we'd sit down and we'd practice these things, you know. And I would say that it more or less was, you'd say, kind of commercial because there were really no real jazz musicians mixed up in this except the fact that we were trying to play and get started. And I played a few jobs like that. And then I think about the first real job professionally that I ever had. I've often referred to another place, which I will tell you about later, but I think this first job that I had was in a neighborhood theater. They called for three pieces, violin, piano, and drums. And of course our job was to play for the silent movies because they had no sound, you know. And this was at a theater called the St. Maurice Avenue Theater, which I think is no longer in existence now. Was that below the bridge?
It was below the bridge, yes.

And I used to ride all the way from Lakeview to St. Maurice Avenue on a streetcar. And we got the big salary of a dollar a piece a night. But of course in those days, you know, a dollar was pretty good, you know. And for a couple of kids, I mean, it looked real good to us. And I guess money was always just secondary, Charlie, if you really loved the music the way we did in those days. I mean, I know it was always that way with me. If I had enough money to navigate on, and I mean, I'd go on jobs and wouldn't even ask, what is it going to pay? Right. All I wanted to know is where was it, how long was it going to be, and all that sort of thing. It's just a little different then. I don't think it's quite that way now. No.
